main_text.p: iudicem, eiusq; iudicium ineuitabile & in stissimū esse. Videmus quàm multi, hoc exulceratissimo rerum humanarum statu, dū φιλήδονοι esse malunt quàm φιλόθεοι, seipsos eant perditum. Nos contrà studeamus esse φιλόθεοι: nec amplius cupiditatibus hominum, sed uoluntati Dei, quod reliquum est temporis in carne uiuamus: ut monet iubetq; Spiritus sanctus, 1. Pet. 4. 2.

Celebratur à Dione Seuerus Imperator, quòd fuerit [?]ἀτιμελὴς τῶν τραχέων, καὶ ἀ-μελὴς τῶν περὶ αὐτὰ λογομαχιῶν. Si laus di ducitur uiro Principi, diligentia in omni officio, & contemtus fabellarum, quæ ab imperita multitudine etiā de optimis Principibus spargi & circumferri solent: multò magis laudi uertendum erit omnium ordinum hominibus, pietatis, uirtutum & erudita doctrina studium. Huius uero studiï (quod à Paulo Apostolo, Dei nomine requiritur illustri hac sententia: τῇ σπουδῇ μὴ ὀκνηροὶ, Studio minimè pigri: Rom. 12. 11.) si Principes, si Comites, si tota Nobilitas ἐργο-διδάσκης sit, & exemplo suo præeat inferioribus, nihil sanè dubium est, magna ex parte hos

page.notes: The first line of the page continues a word from the previous page ("iudicem" is a fragment of "iudicem" in the sentence), so the first paragraph is marked cont="true". The Greek word "ἀτιμελὴς" is doubtful and marked [?]; the Greek on the last lines of the text is not fully legible and was copied as far as possible. The bottom marks "4 6" beside the text are read as a signature and are uncertain. The catchword "hos" is at the right below the last line. No page number is printed.
